findings.desc: concept-cleanup: fetchGateReceiptProof authentication fix incomplete: authority-live-receipt-ref-gate-smoke.ts:860 still calls new AuthorityClient(input.ctx.liveURL).fetchGateReceiptProof(proofPath) with no auth arg (unauthenticated), while ctx.customerApiKey is available in scope (line 151/170). Since the proof endpoint is protected (401 without auth), this diagnostic fetch will 401 in the same conditions the fix is designed to cure — defeating the diagnostic.

quality-cleanup: authority-live-receipt-ref-gate-smoke.ts:860 constructs AuthorityClient without auth for diagnostic proof fetch, but fetchGateReceiptProof now requires authenticated:true — the rich diagnostic branch (proof.ok && proof.data) at line 861 is permanently dead after this fix because the unauthenticated client will always fail closed (kind:error). The diagnostic should pass ctx.customerApiKey as auth to remain useful.

CHK-001:happy:1 evidence note falsely claims schema parse success: the intent requires outcome.ok===true and data matches AuthorityGateReceiptProofSchema, but authority-receipt-proof-auth-smoke.ts line 35 discards the return value of authed.fetchGateReceiptProof() with no assertion on it. The stub body { stub: "not-a-valid-proof" } fails AuthorityGateReceiptProofSchema.safeParse() (returns ok:false, kind:error), so the authenticated read actually does NOT produce a valid parsed proof in the test. The evidence note inference chain ("returns without throwing...proves the happy-path parse") is false: get() never throws on schema failure, it returns ok:false. No test case verifies outcome.ok===true or that valid proof JSON round-trips through the schema.

CHK-002:happy:0 evidence only demonstrates the AuthorityClient constructor pattern in isolation; loadProof() itself is never called in the deterministic smoke. The evidence note says "the loadProof code path uses the same constructor pattern" — this is a structural inference, not an execution trace. The must-priority intent requires proving that loadProof({proofPath:..., authorityURL:...}) with LATTICE_AUTHORITY_CUSTOMER_API_KEY set actually sends Authorization: Bearer <key>. No test calls loadProof() directly; the fix at authority-enforce.ts:206-207 is only verified by code inspection, not by an executing test that exercises loadProof end-to-end through the auth resolution path.
